page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped from a single physical AMD EPYC 9T24 core with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 (Foundation, VNNI, and BF16) for vector and deep learning workloads, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The CPU cache hierarchy consists of a 32 KB L1 data cache, a 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache, which assists in handling instruction-heavy tasks.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, due to its low core count, multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also constrained, with read-only small block bandwidth and database operations scoring in the bottom 10%. Static web serving throughput and Redis SET operations also show poor relative performance.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-thread performance, the ecs.c8a.large offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require consistent CPU performance without massive parallelization. It is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and utility services. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, high-throughput web serving, or highly parallelized compilation tasks.
